UNITED STATES ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY
REGION III 
6TH AND WALNUT STREETS
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA 19106
August 17, 1973
Mr. James Corbin, Director
Community Development Disaster
Recovery Office
U.S. Department of Housing and
Urban Development
Spruce and Adams Avenue
Scranton, Pennsylvania 18503
Re: Urban Renewal Projects in Harrisburg (Penn-Susquehanna), Kingston, Lock Haven, Milton (and Turbot), Reading (Model Citics One), and Wilkes-Barre (Downtown)
Dear Mr. Corbin:
We have completed our review of the draft environmental impact statements for the above disaster recovery Urban Renewal projects. As general descriptions of the various proposed project actions, the draft statements are well done. We are reporting these reviews in EPA reference category LO-2; this indicates our general lack of objections to the projects, as described, and the need for more detailed information in the final statements, as discussed below, to permit a more thorough environmental assessment. The date and classification of EPA's comments will be published in the Federal Register in accordance with our responsibility, under Section 309 of the Clean Air Act, to inform the public of our views on proposed Federal actions. We recognize the need for future determinations of the need for additional impact statements on more specifically-defined housing, transportation, and flood control projects associated with the urban renewal efforts.
Our primary concern with projects of this type is that they, in combination with flood control measures, perpetuate land use situations which have been repeatedly disastrous in the past.
